title: One name per thing: a glossary in every repo
why: Your idea, Oct 26: AI sessions need settled terms. A photos folder beside a captures folder leads to confusion, a second copy being built, and misread asks.
note: Checked Oct 26: no glossary in claude-settings (f463787), banchi (9683902) or home-app (65315da); q_max and home not checked. The only related rule is output-write-in-ste ('one term per meaning'), which governs prose, not names of folders, files, types or concepts. This is the naming side of o11 (one home per shared thing): two names for one thing is how a second home gets built. Advisor pick, not ruled: (1) each repo gets GLOSSARY.md with one row per term: the term, what it means, where it lives (path or symbol), and the names not to use for it ('not: photos, pictures'); only terms that caused or could cause confusion, not a dictionary. (2) One rule in claude-settings: before naming a new folder, file, type, setting or concept, check the glossary and reuse its term; a new term gets its row in the same change; renaming to the glossary term beats adding a second name. CLAUDE.md points at the file and does not inline it (token cost). (3) Later, a CI lint (CI only, per c21) that fails a new path or symbol matching a 'not:' name; build it only after a real repeat. (4) o2 (one layout) puts GLOSSARY.md in the shared layout; each repo seeds it from its known clashes. Unknown: which repo has the photos/captures clash. Web check, Oct 26: the idea is DDD's 'ubiquitous language' (one shared vocabulary, used in talk and in code). Agent skills already do it: mattpocock/skills 'ubiquitous-language' (skills.sh/mattpocock/skills/ubiquitous-language) writes UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md from a conversation and flags one word for several things, several words for one thing, and vague terms. Prose linters enforce preferred terms in CI with a substitution list (Vale; posthog.com/handbook/docs-and-wizard/vale, elastic/vale-rules). Known pitfalls (archman.dev/docs/domain-driven-design/strategic-design/ubiquitous-language): a glossary written once goes stale; code names drift from the glossary; a term can mean different things in different parts of a system (so one row per repo, not one global list); little value for small or early-prototype projects. Fit here: the stale risk is the main one; a 'not:' list that a lint reads stays alive, and terms named in code paths can be checked to exist. Your word, Oct 26: agreed on GLOSSARY.md; claude-settings holds only terms that matter in every repo, each repo its own domain terms (a photos/captures clash is a repo row, never claude-settings'). Shape, advisor pick: (a) claude-settings GLOSSARY.md, installed beside the global CLAUDE.md and pointed at, not inlined: the workflow nouns every session meets (lane, batch, integration PR, clone, pin, live link, worktree, handoff, goal, step, ruling, decision, debt, note, record, guard, gate, check, advisor, owner, override pass). (b) Each repo's GLOSSARY.md: its domain terms. A repo never redefines a global term; on a clash the repo renames. (c) Agent and skill edits: Plan lists the new names a plan introduces and checks them against both glossaries; builder reuses glossary terms and adds a row in the same change as a new name; reviewer flags a new name that duplicates an existing term or lacks its row; record-writer uses the terms; a small glossary skill seeds a repo's file from its tree and docs and proposes rows (run at rollout and on demand); compliance-check (o4) checks the file exists. (d) Staleness check in CI, cheap: every row's 'lives at' path still exists, and no new path uses a 'not:' name. (e) o2 puts GLOSSARY.md in the shared layout.
